Criteria: aesthetic and story fit, zone representation, readability and fairness from the isometric camera (parry timing), mechanical depth with existing verbs, spectacle, buildability (Blender script + Unity), and animation potential. All 0-10.

CONCEPT A: "Mizuchi, el Gran Koi" (boss-water-0). Average 8.6.
- Fit 8.5.
  - For: Tancho koi, shimenawa and the Dragon Gate legend (koi no takinobori) are iconic, and white/red on dark moonlit water matches "vibrant but dark" plus moonlight.
  - For: the waterfall becomes the boss's motive, the phase-change set piece and the ending. The golden-dragon ending ties into the yellow HUD dragon the user loves.
  - Against: it reframes the platform as a festival shrine, while the design doc lists a "Dojo de Jefe del Lago" (easy to reconcile).
  - Against: its reveal "Yo también fui un koi", spoken by the Bandana Spirit, contradicts StoryText ("el espíritu del abuelo me habla"). Fixed in the synthesis.
- Zone 10. It is literally the lake's lord, and it wants the waterfall.
- Readability 8.
  - For: 380-560 px long at game scale, with 6 clearly different state silhouettes (poses_sheet.png, koi_game_*.png).
  - For: the red tancho disc always marks the head and bite direction.
  - For: a reasoned constant 0.33 s cue against parryWindow 0.24 / perfect 0.11.
  - Against: player hits test e.transform.position plus Radius (PlayerController.Combat.cs:123), so a 7.5 m body can't be hit at the tail. Needs a hurt segment.
  - Against: in "Pilares" the koi hangs 14 m up in the curtain. I computed it is off-screen: at combat pitch 43, distance 28 and FOV 30, a point 13 m north of the focus is visible only up to about 1.3-2.4 m height, and only about 2.9 m even with the proposed 8 degree tilt.
  - Against: 5 unblockables, while dash costs 15 Spirit (PlayerConfig.cs:59).
- Depth 8. Positional play (flank vs tail whip), pearls that teach the perfect parry, and line/ring dodges. The parry duel itself is thinner than B's.
- Spectacle 10.
- Buildability 7.
  - For: the non-humanoid rig needs no IK.
  - For: its 2-child Hover/Swim locomotion fits generate_assets.controller() (line 349) unchanged.
  - For: the falls sit as a landmark inside the existing LAKE polygon, with no terrain edit.
  - Against: 8 new specials with off-NavMesh movement; about 15 days for the full version.
- Animation potential 9. Fish motion is a travelling wave plus spring overlap, which scripted per-frame baking does very well. It is exactly "realistic motion on a clearly non-realistic character".

CONCEPT B: "Sayo / La Espada bajo la Cascada" (boss-water-1). Average 7.0.
- Fit 8.
  - For: matches the doc's lake-boss dojo; the takigyō / yūrei idea is lovely; good voseo dialogue and a humane ending.
  - Against: a 4th sword-wielding humanoid (ninjas, Gorō, Kage).
- Zone 7. Water lives mostly in VFX and costume.
- Readability 6.
  - She is about 70 px tall and a 40 px hat disc dominates. Pose changes from above are subtle (sheet_game_crop.png), and the blade is 3-5 px wide.
  - The groove-fill and hat-tilt tells are clever but lean on decals.
  - Its white "parry" decal conflicts with the shipped CombatTelegraphs grammar (gold = parry, red = dash; CombatTelegraphs.cs).
- Depth 9. The best parry duel: Nagashi counter-stance, the kingfisher double, a delayed third hit, a reflectable crescent and the volley rally.
- Spectacle 7. The wave and Takigiri are strong, but the boss herself is small on screen.
- Buildability 5.5.
  - 29 clips of scripted humanoid swordplay through an IK control rig. Its own prototype already shows the blade tip 0.83 m under the floor and a 106 m/s one-frame jump.
  - It needs a LAKE polygon cut and a plateau rule in world_terrain, an N-child blend-tree extension and 8 new palette swatches.
- Animation potential 6.5. The principles are excellent, but scripted humanoid katana arcs are the hardest thing to make look professional. That is exactly what the user is unhappy with.

VERDICT: build A, grafting B's best ideas. B contributes:
- the "el agua no miente" telegraph tutorial;
- the Tama-asobi rally;
- the phase-2 flood sheet;
- the mist clearing around the fighters and dithered spray blobs;
- the nested ribbon curtain with time-of-flight UVs and posterized 3-tone;
- the impact-crown sub-emitter;
- moonbow placement at the anti-moon point;
- FacingProbe plus anim_lint (with the run-direction lint for every character);
- the noRecoil flag, a bigger boss glint, music stems per phase, Shigure-style risk/reward;
- falls placed due north, so the camera yaw stays 0.
chosen:
Concept A, "Mizuchi, el Gran Koi" (boss-water-0), synthesized with grafts from Concept B (Sayo).

The judge also made these corrections:
- **Falls placement:** the falls go due NORTH of the arena, and the camera yaw stays 0 in the boss arena. No 45-degree sub-zone rotation of the input basis.
- **Telegraphs:** extend the existing CombatTelegraphs (gold = parry, red = dash) instead of adding a new GroundTelegraph class.
- **Pilares:** performed from the deck, so the boss is never off-screen during an attack.
- **Fairness rule:** every unblockable has a non-dash answer.
- **Hitbox:** a hurt segment for the long body.
- **Animation timing:** the boss's attacks use flat timing (no Snappy curve), so authored strikes are not re-timed.
- **Lore:** the HUD dragon is a koi the grandfather once helped. The Bandana Spirit is not itself a koi.

final.pitch:
WHAT IT IS
- Mizuchi is the Nushi (ancient lord) of Lake Kohan: a 7.5 m Tancho-Kohaku koi spirit that swims through the air over Kohanoie's floating dojo-shrine.
- The platform sits at the foot of the Kohan Falls, a 42 m horseshoe waterfall. For centuries the koi has tried to climb it to become a dragon: the real Japanese legend of the Dragon Gate, 'koi no takinobori'.
- The Kurokage clan drove the Water Seal into its back as an iron stake, so it can no longer climb and it attacks anyone on the platform.
- Kaito's goal is to FREE it, not kill it. Beaten and beached, the koi loses the stake to the finisher. It climbs the falls and rises as the golden dragon, the same dragon as the HUD Spirit bar.

WHY IT WORKS
- The waterfall is not a backdrop. It is the boss's motive, the phase-2 transformation and the ending.
- Koi are bred to be admired from above. A single red disc on the white head always shows where the head (and the bite) is, from Nindō's high camera.
- It moves like a real fish on a creature that is clearly not real, which is exactly what the user asked for:
  - C-start wind-ups, S-snap strikes, a travelling-wave swim;
  - spring follow-through on fins and whiskers;
  - a flopping, beached exhausted state.
- It answers 'I don't know WHEN to parry' with one consistent grammar, taught in-world by the Bandana Spirit ('El agua no miente'):
  - Gold water = parry. The existing CombatTelegraphs ring closes on contact; a gold glint and a water-chime fire exactly 0.33 s before contact.
  - Red water = get out. A red ground shape appears at least 0.9 s ahead with a taiko 'don'; a red glint and a 'ka!' come 0.33 s before.
  - Every red attack can be escaped by running (dash costs 15 Spirit). Dash is the stylish answer: 'Instante sombra'.
- It gives the game one creature boss among humanoids (ninjas, Gorō, Ōzeki, Kage).

JUDGE'S CORRECTIONS TO THE BASE CONCEPT
1. **Falls placement:** the falls sit due north of the arena. The camera yaw stays 0 (world_plan.py header: 'La cámara mira hacia el norte'), so the input basis never rotates mid-fight. The moon (Euler 48,-38,0) front-lights the south-facing curtain, and the anti-moon point lands in the plunge spray, which is where a moonbow physically forms.
2. **No off-screen attacks:** the koi never leaves the gameplay frame during an attack. 'ClimbFalls' is cutscene-only, and Pilares is cast from the deck.
3. **Telegraphs:** extend the shipped CombatTelegraphs (commit d9c23df) with world-anchored shapes. No parallel system and no white parry colour.
4. **Hitbox:** a hurt segment (Enemy.HurtCenter) so Kaito can hit the whole 7.5 m body.
5. **Lore:** the Bandana Spirit is the grandfather's spirit. The HUD dragon is a koi the grandfather once helped climb these falls.
final.lore:
KOHANOIE AND THE FALLS
- Kohanoie is a village of fishermen on stilts over Lake Kohan.
- At the lake's north end the Kohan river drops 42 m over a horseshoe of basalt columns: the Kohan Falls.
- At their foot stands the village's octagonal floating dojo-shrine (today's lake_arena_platform; the design doc's 'Dojo de Jefe del Lago'). There:
  - swordsmen did takigyō under the spray (graft from Concept B);
  - every full moon the village lit the lanterns and beat taiko for the Takinobori-matsuri, while the Great Koi tried to climb the falls.
- The koi always fell a few metres short and never stopped trying. For the village it means perseverance.
- A small waterfall shrine with a shimenawa rope stands on a ledge at the foot of the west cliff.

THE CRIME
- To lock the dojo gate the Kurokage needed a guardian per seal.
- At the lake they drove the Water Seal, as an iron stake, into the koi's back. The stake carries the key_seal_lake medallion design at 2.5x, wrapped in shimenawa with a black clan crest. No kanji anywhere.
- The koi can no longer climb. Corruption spreads from the stake and turns its scales black when it is enraged.
- The lake went dark and the lanterns went out. The fishermen hang their nets on the net_racks and stopped fishing. Whoever steps onto the platform is attacked.

THE FIGHT AND ITS MEANING
- Kaito breaks its strength (beached, flopping). The finisher cuts the shimenawa and the stake shoots out.
- The ink flakes off and the koi turns pure white. It swims up the falls and, at the lip, becomes Mizuchi: a golden dragon rising into the moon.
- The seal, now glowing clean cyan, falls onto the platform.
- Theme: the game's line is 'el camino ninja no se recorre solo'. The koi failed alone for centuries and rises only because someone helped it. That is the opposite of Kage, who chose to walk alone.
- Reveal (corrected so it stays consistent with StoryText, where the Spirit is the grandfather's): long ago the grandfather helped another koi climb these falls, and that dragon lives in the bandana. This explains why the Spirit bar is a dragon, and the HUD dragon can play a special coil animation when the seal is picked up.

IN-GAME TEXT (Spanish, voseo; paste into StoryText)
- mizuchi_intro (replaces StoryText.cs:162-165):
  L('Espíritu de la Bandana', 'Ese koi lleva siglos intentando remontar la cascada... y el clan le clavó el sello en el lomo.')
  L(Kaito, 'Por eso el lago está oscuro. Aguantá, gran koi: te voy a sacar esa estaca.')
  L('Espíritu de la Bandana', 'Mirá el agua, Kaito. El agua no miente: dorada, desviá. Roja, salí de ahí.')
- Phase 2 toast: '¡El sello corrompe a Mizuchi!'
- Phase 3 toast: '¡La cascada responde!'
- Defeat toast, for this boss instead of '{title} derrotado': 'Mizuchi, liberado'
- seal_lake (replaces StoryText.cs:178-179):
  L(Kaito, 'El Sello del Agua... y el koi, por fin libre.')
  L('Espíritu de la Bandana', 'Hace mucho, tu abuelo ayudó a otro koi a subir esta cascada. Ese dragón vive en tu bandana.')
- New sub-zone 'lago_cascada': title 'Cascada Kohan', subtitle 'Donde los koi se vuelven dragones' (no kanji field; ShowAreaTitle is already kanji-free).

AFTERMATH (flag boss_mizuchi)
- Lake fog density -20%.
- The platform's 4 stone lanterns light up (emissive on).
- The falls calm to intensity 0.8.
- Optional: 2 fishermen NPCs on the docks say 'El koi subió la cascada... por fin.'
final.look:
PROPORTIONS (prototype koi_proto.py, renders2/*.png, poses_sheet.png)
- Length 7.5 m from snout to the tips of the tail fan; body 5.7 m; girth 1.95 m wide x 1.95 m tall at 1.1 m behind the head.
- Pectoral span 4.7 m; tail fan 3.1 m.
- Hover: belly 0.76 m above the deck; body axis at 1.62 m (about Kaito's head height); back at 2.7 m; dorsal top 3.43 m.
- Against Kaito (1.5 m): five times his length, twice his height. On the 21 m platform (circumradius 10.6) it leaves about 6 m of deck on each side.

CARICATURE (design doc: 'caricature anatomy, readable details')
- Head 27% of body length; humped back; short body.
- Oversized hirenaga butterfly fins.
- Twin fan tail splayed 55 degrees from vertical, so it reads as a wide fan from above (a vertical tail is a 4 cm line in the top view).

PARTS
- Body loft, 16 sides x 22 rings. Every other ring is twisted half a step, so the flat facets form diamond scales: the low-poly faceting IS the scale pattern.
- Protrusible lip ring, 2 gold eyes, 2 gill plates, 2 barbel pairs.
- Long pleated pectoral fans (alternating light and dark rays under flat shading); pelvic and anal fins; ragged dorsal sail; twin fan tail.
- Shimenawa rope belt with 3 shide streamers per side.
- On the back, the iron stake topped by the Water Seal medallion (radius 0.34 m).
- NEW 'Ripple' disc, radius 2.5 m, flat at deck level, skinned 100% to root. It is the 'water mirror' ground anchor that reads the hover height from above. Because NormalizeHeight (CharacterFactory.cs:115) puts the lowest vertex at y = 0, it also preserves the hover with zero code. KoiBody swaps its material at runtime to transparent glow_water at 30%.
- NEW 'FacingProbe' bone (see rig).

PALETTE (existing nindo_palette names only; no new swatches)
- Phase 1 'Tancho':
  - Scales alternate white #f4f4f0 and plaster #e6dcc8; belly plaster_shade #bfb39c.
  - ONE red disc on top of the head, flower_red #d6453a, enlarged to 1.1 m (about 80 px at game scale; the 0.9 m prototype disc reads small in koi_game_neutral.png). It is the head and bite-direction marker and the only red on the body.
  - Gin-rin scales: glow_moon #cfe6ff emissive on about 3.5% of the upper scales.
  - Fins: water_foam #cfe7ec / white pleats with ONLY the outer 10% rim in glow_water #7ff0e0 (the prototype's fully glowing fins overpowered everything).
  - Eyes gold #d9a93a with black #1c1c20 pupils; mouth clay_dark #7a4a30.
  - Rope #c9b27a / straw #d2bd80; shide paper #efe3c6; stake iron #4a4d52.
  - Medallion: gold rim, water_deep #1f4a5e centre, glow_purple #c08aff corruption glow, plus a pulsing purple point light (intensity 1.5, range 5) that marks the boss in the dark.
- Phase 2 'Corrupted':
  - Body ink #22252a / cloth_black #26262c; belly stone_dark #5f615f.
  - glow_purple crack veins radiating from the stake; eyes glow_red #ff4a3a.
  - Coral horns, 1 m long, in wood_red_dark #6e1d1b with glow_red tips.
  - Whiskers 3.2 m long in glow_purple; taller, bristling dorsal mane.
  - Fins ink / cloth_purple #5b3a6b with a glow_purple rim.
  - White to black-and-purple is the strongest phase read possible from above (koi_hero_p2.png).
- Freed (ending only): the phase-2 shape (horns and whiskers, so a dragon) rendered with FXMaterials.Ghost additive tinted glow_spirit #ffd86b, the HUD dragon's gold.
- Night-read check: under moonlight the white body renders grey-blue (koi_hero_p1.png). It is carried by the cool falls fill light (rim from the north) and Kaito's MoonLantern.
  - Acceptance test: in a Unity capture, the body's mean luminance is at least 1.8x the deck planks'.
  - If it fails, raise the gin-rin emissive share to 6% rather than adding flat emission.

MATERIALS
- Nindo palette atlas with 2 slots (Nindo_Palette, Nindo_Emissive); flat shading; no textures, so it batches with the world.
- HitFlash and CharacterFactory.Tint still work. Tint strength 0: remove today's blue tint at EnemyArchetypes.cs:154.

POLY BUDGET
- Team references (measured): Kaito 6,100 tris / 62 bones; ninja 6,022 / 65; Gorō 7,477 / 65; grandpa 6,973 / 82.
- Body_P1 about 2,700 tris; Body_P2 about 3,100; Ripple 32. Only one body is visible at a time.
- 40 bones.

READABILITY AT GAME SCALE (arena camera pitch 43, about 28 m, FOV 30, 1080p, about 75 px/m)
- Koi 380-560 px long; tancho about 80 px; fin blades about 150 px; Kaito about 110 px.
- Four reads from above: the red disc (head, bite direction); two pale blade fins; the wide fan tail; the glowing purple seal (the curse and the finisher point).
- Each state has its own silhouette (poses_sheet.png): straight = neutral; C-curl = bite wind-up; S = strike; tight C = tail whip; detached shadow = leap; on its side = beached.
final.rig:
BUILT BY SCRIPT
- New Tools/Blender/characters/build_mizuchi.py, grown from scratch koi_proto.py, which already does steps 1-3 at low density.
- Deterministic; no auto-weights.
- Run: blender -b --factory-startup --python build_mizuchi.py -- <out.fbx> [preview.png]

1. BONES FROM A TABLE
- Each entry gives head, tail and parent. edit_bones are created with roll 0 and use_connect False.
- Every chain bone lies along ±Y, so local Z is about world up. One convention for poses and for Unity: yaw = local Z, pitch = local X, roll = local Y.
- The front chain points -Y (toward the head) and the back chain +Y.
- A C-curl therefore needs opposite signs on the two chains (front +a, back -a); the same sign gives an S. This was the prototype's fixed bug.

2. MESH
- bmesh builds Body_P1 and Body_P2 (the seal parts are inside both, on bone 'seal') plus Ripple. Vertices are weighted when they are created, through the deform layer:
  - Spine: smoothstep blend between the two nearest spine-bone centres along Y (head -2.0, spine_f -0.9, body -0.05, b1 0.62, b2 1.35, b3 2.0, b4 2.5, tail 2.95).
  - Fins: by t along the fin (bone1 = 1 - 1.4t, bone2 = 1.4t; the third bone takes t > 0.7).
  - Lips: 70% jaw / 30% head.
  - Barbel and horn segments: rigid.
  - Dorsal: spine weight x (1 - t) + dorsal bone x t.
  - Stake and medallion: 100% seal. Ripple: 100% root.

3. ARMATURE
- Armature modifier, then parent the meshes to 'MizuchiRig'.

HIERARCHY (40 bones; Blender metres, head -> tail; character faces -Y)
- root (0,0,0)->(0,0.6,0). Gameplay origin on the deck; no horizontal translation in clips.
  - FacingProbe (0,-3.0,1.62)->(0,-3.3,1.62). DEFORM with no weights, so use_armature_deform_only exports it. It must import at Unity local +Z.
  - body (0,-0.35,1.62)->(0,0.25,1.62). Centre of gravity: bob, roll, pitch, the 360-degree whip spin, lunges up to 1.2 m.
- FRONT CHAIN, under body:
  - spine_f (0,-0.35,1.62)->(0,-1.35,1.62)
    - head (0,-1.35,1.62)->(0,-2.55,1.5)
      - jaw (0,-2.05,1.32)->(0,-2.7,1.3). Opens and slides forward 0.28 m (the protrusible carp mouth).
        - barbel_L1 (0.26,-2.42,1.36)->(0.42,-2.75,1.18) -> barbel_L2 ->(0.55,-2.95,0.98) -> barbel_L3 ->(0.62,-3.2,0.85); barbel_R1-R3 mirrored. L3/R3 skin only the phase-2 whiskers.
      - gill_L (0.7,-1.5,1.5)->(0.85,-1.1,1.4); gill_R mirrored.
      - horn_L (0.32,-1.75,2.2)->(0.6,-0.8,3.2); horn_R mirrored. Phase-2 mesh only; keep the horn top (3.2) below the dorsal top (3.43) so NormalizeHeight is the same for both phases.
      - eye_glint (0,-1.8,2.45)->(0,-1.8,2.75). On the tancho disc: glint point for the Bite, anchor for the lock-on reticle and the imbalance pips.
    - pec_L1 (0.72,-1.15,1.12)->(1.45,-0.75,0.92) -> pec_L2 ->(2.0,-0.35,0.82) -> pec_L3 ->(2.35,-0.05,0.75); pec_R1-R3 mirrored.
  - seal (0,-0.3,2.62)->(0,-0.3,3.15)
  - dorsal_1 (0,-0.7,2.6)->(0,-0.7,3.2)
- BACK CHAIN, under body:
  - spine_b1 (0,0.25,1.62)->(0,1.0,1.63) -> spine_b2 ->(0,1.7,1.65) -> spine_b3 ->(0,2.3,1.67) -> spine_b4 ->(0,2.75,1.69) -> tail ->(0,3.1,1.71)
  - on spine_b1: dorsal_2 (0,0.3,2.5)->(0,0.3,3.0); pel_L (0.42,0.55,0.85)->(0.75,1.15,0.55); pel_R mirrored
  - on spine_b2: dorsal_3 (0,1.1,2.3)->(0,1.1,2.75)
  - on spine_b3: dorsal_4 (0,1.8,2.15)->(0,1.8,2.5); anal (0,1.85,1.05)->(0,2.3,0.75)
  - on tail: fluke_L1 (0.1,3.0,1.72)->(0.75,3.8,1.85) -> fluke_L2 ->(1.35,4.6,1.9); fluke_R1-R2 mirrored

FACING GUARD (so the 'Kaito runs sideways' class of bug cannot reach the game)
- In Blender, before export, assert:
  - head.tail.y < tail.tail.y;
  - eye_glint.y < 0;
  - FacingProbe.y < 0.
- With axis_forward '-Z' and axis_up 'Y', Blender -Y becomes Unity +Z (nindo_lib.blender_to_unity_vec = [-x, z, -y]), so modelYaw = 0.
- In Unity, a new NindoContentTools validator instantiates every CharacterEntry and applies modelYaw. It requires the 'FacingProbe' bone (or, for team rigs, the head's forward offset from the hips) to point to +Z within 15 degrees. It runs on every regeneration of NindoContent.

EXPORT
- One FBX: Nindo/Assets/Nindo/Art/Models/Characters/Mizuchi.fbx (armature, Body_P1, Body_P2, Ripple).
- object_types {ARMATURE, MESH}; use_armature_deform_only True; add_leaf_bones False; primary_bone_axis 'Y'; secondary_bone_axis 'X'.
- apply_unit_scale; apply_scale_options 'FBX_SCALE_UNITS'; mesh_smooth_type 'FACE'.
- bake_anim True; bake_anim_use_all_actions True (takes 'MizuchiRig|<Clip>'); bake_anim_use_nla_strips False; bake_anim_force_startend_keying True; bake_anim_step 1.
- bake_anim_simplify_factor 0.0. export_grandpa.py uses 0.5, which would soften the 2-frame snaps.
- Sidecar Mizuchi.fbx.json: {clips:[{name, take, first, last, loop, contactFrame, holdFrame}]}. Frames are stored in FBX time; the B prototype's round trip shifted keys 0-27 to 1-28, so check stateLengths in Unity.
- Unity import: Generic (animationType 2), no root motion, animation compression OFF (or Keyframe Reduction with rotation error 0.2 degrees or less) so the 2-frame snaps survive.

UNITY PROCEDURAL LAYER (new KoiBody.cs, LateUpdate after the Animator, purely additive)
- Each bone's axis = Quaternion.Inverse(bone.rotation) * Vector3.up, so it is independent of FBX bone axes.
- Spine-follow: keep 1 s of root-yaw history. spine_b1..tail get yaw(t - 0.05(i+1)) - yaw(t), clamped to ±30 degrees, with weights 0.35 / 0.5 / 0.65 / 0.8 / 0.9 times the locomotion weight. Turns bend the body and the tail follows the head's path.
- Bank: roll = clamp(yawRate x 0.08, ±20 degrees).
- Head look-at toward Kaito within ±25 degrees (head 0.6, spine_f 0.4) in Locomotion and Guard.
- All weights fade to 0 within 0.1 s during attack steps, so authored strikes are never altered.
- It also handles: the phase-1/phase-2 renderer swap, the Ripple material, the seal light pulse, and a Hurt polyline (live positions of head, spine_b1, spine_b3) read by MizuchiBoss.HurtCenter.
final.animations:
21 CLIPS AT 30 FPS, keyed by script in the new Tools/Blender/characters/mizuchi_anims.py.

AUTHORING
- A pose library ({bone: (rx, ry, rz)} in degrees, bone-local) and per-clip key lists [(frame, pose, interp)].
- Interpolation presets: 'snap' = EXPO ease-out, 'settle' = BACK ease-out (1.2), 'hold' = SINE in-out, 'ease' = QUAD in-out.
- Three procedural layers are baked per frame on top of the keys:
  (a) Travelling wave on the spine: phase step 0.9 rad per bone; small at the head and large at the tail (the carangiform envelope).
  (b) Spring-damper secondary motion (k = 60, c = 8) on pec_*2/3, pel_*, dorsal_*, anal, fluke_*, barbel_*. Simulated from each parent's angular acceleration with 2 warm-up loops for cyclic clips. This gives automatic overlap and follow-through.
  (c) Noise for moving holds and roars.
- Unity side: these clips use FLAT timing (AttackDef.timing = null). The existing Hit() helper always applies Snappy(0.85, 1.35) (EnemyArchetypes.cs:19), which would double-snap authored strikes and move contact off the authored frame.

TIMING RULE (with the hold fix in implementation step A1)
- Contact time = activeStart x L + 0.85 x telegraph.
- The held 'coil' pose sits at frame holdFrame, and AttackDef.holdAt = holdFrame / frames.
- Only about 1 frame of clip advances during the hold (15% speed). The snap occupies the last 2-4 frames before contact.

ANIM LINT (new shared Tools/Blender/characters/anim_lint.py; it fails the export and prints the frame and bone)
- (a) Facing probe.
- (b) Contact frame = round(activeStart x frames) for every attack.
- (c) Anticipation : strike : recovery about 55 : 8 : 37 for parryable attacks.
- (d) Main-bone snaps last 2-3 frames; children trail by 1-2 frames.
- (e) Holds are never frozen: ±1-2 degree drift inside the hold window, and under 40 degrees/s there.
- (f) root never moves horizontally; body moves at most 1.2 m.
- (g) No vertex below the deck except in Exhausted, BreachLand and Dive.
- (h) Angular-speed spike detector to catch pops.
- (i) For any biped run take (also run it on the team FBX takes): the average foot-contact velocity must point backward. This catches 'running sideways'.
